first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Both memory_31 and memory_86 show that streamlining the onboarding process—cutting required fields and shortening flows—produce durable lifts in early activation and adoption. These are directly addressable pain points with proven solutions in our own history. While promotional_pricing could address the competitive threat, it risks a race to the bottom and lower-quality revenue. Simplifying onboarding addresses the measurable internal degradation, improves the core experience for all segments (SMB and enterprise), and compounds with memory_91's activation messaging for greater impact. Verifying memory_31 and memory_86 confirms the magnitude and durability of the prior lifts before committing resources. A standard experiment allows controlled rollout with measurement.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both prior experiments. memory_31 delivered +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with only -1% retention impact. memory_86 delivered +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value improvement, and +3% retention lift. Combined, these show that onboarding simplification is a high-confidence lever for activation recovery. The 4% QoQ completion decline and 6% activation decline align directly with what these interventions address. Unlike promotional pricing (which risks revenue quality and competitive spiral) or referral incentives (which require existing customer base momentum we lack), onboarding improvements compound across all segments and preserve long-term unit economics. memory_91 (activation messaging) suggests further gains are possible when combined. Standard experiment scope allows safe validation before broad rollout, maintaining uncertainty where appropriate and protecting qualified revenue as primary objective.
